correctness.rationale: In KG(6,2), a connected induced triple is either a perfect-matching triangle (15 choices) or a two-edge path (180 triangles in ten complementary 3+3 partition blocks). The Alexander dual K of ordinary three-cut X has 15 vertices, 105 edges, 195 triangles and 90 tetrahedra, with no 5-vertex face. Every tetrahedron belongs to one of ten explicit joins ∂Δ²*∂Δ² ≅S³ whose 2-face supports are pairwise disjoint. Each 9-tetrahedron sphere boundary has rank8 primitive image, giving H3(K)=Z10 and torsion-free H2. Every missing triangle has union of ground labels of size at most four, so a complementary 2-subset w cones its boundary using three allowed triangles; π1(K)=0, hence H1=0. Euler reduced χ=14 implies H2(K)=Z24. Integral Alexander duality on 15 vertices and full 9-skeleton of X imply H9(X)=Z10,H10(X)=Z24 and X is 8-connected; Hurewicz and homological Whitehead yield wedge 10S9∨24S10. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all 2^15 subsets reproduced block decomposition, 260 missing-triangle cones and skeleton; no modular rank test was used as sole proof of torsion-freeness.
